doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Final advice: stay with the music
summary: Liston says to study and do it or not, not to get hung up on people before lifelong love, and that she kept to her music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: If they’re going to study and do it, do it.
And if not, don’t do it.
That’s all I can say. Don’t get all hung up with nobody other than your music
Let that be your old man or your old woman or whatever.
Until you know that somebody that’s going to be yours and you’re going to be his, and you’re going to be lifetime or something together.

And that is a hard nut to crack, learning the difference between lust and love. I have to go through that with my kids, my son. It’s hard. Especially being in show business. You know how everybody’s – we’ve been there.
But I didn’t do a lot of things. Two guys are kind of [?], but other than that, I was not being low or something, and we made it for years, or something like that.
